correctness.rationale: For fixed L and interior u=x/L, subtract C from 1-u to obtain homogeneous Dirichlet heat evolution of 1-u. The killed heat kernel is positive and the first sine coefficient is 2/π; the higher modes decay strictly faster, giving the claimed strict stationary bound and leading exponential. With F=erf(x/sqrt(2t)) and H=F(t,L), the shortcut's heat residual is FH'/H²<0. Duhamel gives strict undershoot: the initial term started at positive ε tends to zero by boundedness and dominated convergence against the heat kernel as ε↓0, so the incompatible initial corner does not supply an extra term. Positivity of the shortcut follows from 0<F<H, and its difference from C is strictly smaller than its difference from stationarity. I independently checked the expansion of erf(uy)/erf(y) through order y² with y=L/sqrt(2t), and the cubic's Poisson equation and boundary values, in symbolic arithmetic. The O(t^-2) tail error is integrable, and termwise time integration of the exact sine series has an absolutely summable n^-3 bound. These are continuum equal-time relaxation integrals, not autocorrelation times. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed; its toleranced sign tests are finite corroboration only.
